title: Porcelain Veneers
meta_title: Porcelain Veneers in Alexandria, VA | West Alexandria Dental Care
meta_description: Porcelain veneers at West Alexandria Dental Care: what they fix, the planning and two-visit process, how much enamel is removed and why it is a commitment.
intro: A veneer is a thin shell of porcelain bonded to the front of a tooth to change its color, shape, length or alignment, or all four at once. Done well on the right teeth, veneers are the most natural-looking and longest-lasting cosmetic change there is. They are also a commitment, because a thin layer of enamel is removed to make room, and we want you to decide with that clearly in view.

sections.heading: What veneers can change
items: Teeth that are permanently discolored and do not respond to whitening.
Chips, worn edges and uneven lengths across several front teeth.
Small gaps and minor crowding or rotation, without orthodontics.
Teeth that are too small, narrow or oddly shaped.
Old, stained bonding across the front teeth that you would like replaced with something more durable.

items.title: Consultation and photographs
items.body: What you want to change, what the teeth and gums allow, and whether a simpler route such as whitening, bonding or aligners would get you there. Health comes first: decay, gum disease and grinding are addressed before veneers are planned.

items.title: Planning the result
items.body: Photographs, models and often a wax-up or mock-up on your own teeth so you can see the proposed shape and length in your mouth before any enamel is touched.

items.title: Preparation
items.body: Under local anesthetic, a thin layer of enamel, roughly the thickness of a fingernail, is removed from the front and edge of each tooth so the veneer sits flush. An impression is taken with a shade match, and temporary veneers are placed.

items.title: Laboratory
items.body: A ceramist makes each veneer in layered porcelain to match the shade, translucency and surface texture of natural teeth. This takes about two weeks.

items.title: Bonding
items.body: The temporaries come off, each veneer is tried in and checked with you in a mirror, then bonded with a resin cement that sets under a light. The bite is adjusted and the edges polished.

sections.heading: Why it is a commitment
body: Enamel does not grow back. Once a tooth has been prepared for a veneer, it will always need a veneer or a crown. That is not a reason to avoid them; it is a reason to be sure. It is why we start with the conservative options, why we mock up the result before preparing anything, and why we say plainly when bonding or aligners would serve you nearly as well without the trade-off.
Some cases suit very thin veneers with minimal or no preparation. Whether yours does depends on the position and color of your teeth, and we tell you honestly rather than promise it.

sections.heading: Caring for veneers
items: Brush and floss as you would natural teeth; the tooth under the veneer can still decay at the edges.
Wear a night guard if you grind. Porcelain is strong but a grinding habit will eventually chip or crack it.
Do not bite fingernails, ice, pens or packaging with the front teeth.
Keep up check-ups so the edges and the gum line are checked and polished.
Whiten the neighboring teeth before veneers are made, not after, so the shade is matched to the final color.

sections.heading: Cost and insurance
sections.body: Veneers are laboratory-made and priced per tooth; the number of teeth and the complexity of the case set the total, and you receive it in writing at the consultation. Insurance almost never covers veneers, because they are cosmetic. Where a veneer or crown is restoring a broken tooth, part may be covered, and we check.

faqs.q: How many veneers do I need?
faqs.a: It depends on how many teeth show when you smile and which ones you want to change. Some people need one veneer to match a single odd tooth; others choose six to ten across the front for a complete change. We show you both options in the mock-up.

Badly made ones do: too white, too flat, too uniform. Well-made veneers are layered to mimic enamel, shaped individually and matched to your face and age. The mock-up stage is where we agree on a result that looks like your teeth, only better.
Preparation is done under local anesthetic. Teeth can be sensitive for a few days with the temporaries and briefly after bonding; that settles.
Rarely, with modern bonding. If one does, keep it and call; it can often be re-bonded. A chipped veneer can sometimes be repaired and sometimes needs replacing.

faqs.q: Are there alternatives if I do not want enamel removed?
faqs.a: Yes. Whitening for color, bonding for chips and gaps, and clear aligners for alignment each avoid removing enamel. Minimal-preparation veneers suit some cases. We go through all of them before anything is decided.

cta.heading: See the result before a single tooth is touched.
cta.body: Book a cosmetic consultation. We photograph, plan and mock up the change on your own teeth, and you decide with the cost in writing.
